audit_2026_10_18: Source audit (live CKAN datastore, 2026-10-18): dataset `approved-building-permits` on data.boston.gov, publisher City of Boston Inspectional Services Department; 666,457 rows all-time (issued permits, 2009-present; applications in process and denied/deleted/void/revoked permits are excluded by the publisher). Trailing-12-month window on issued_date >= 2025-10-17: 36,367 rows = 36,367 distinct permitnumber = 36,367 distinct datastore _id. All-time the table carries 666,457 rows vs 666,444 distinct permit numbers: 13 surplus legacy rows, none in the window. Window statuses: Open 22,225 / Closed 14,142 (the only two values). Window permit types: Short Form Bldg Permit 10,885; Electrical Permit 8,735; Plumbing Permit 5,099; Gas Permit 3,062; Long Form/Alteration Permit 2,720; Electrical Low Voltage 2,081; Electrical Fire Alarms 1,671; Certificate of Occupancy 1,153; Electrical Temporary Service 408; Amendment to a Long Form 320; Erect/New Construction 155; Use of Premises 49; Foundation Permit 29. September 2026 source count: 3,145 permits, declared-valuation sum $1,462,223,768.55 (cross-check targets). VALUATION (declared_valuation, a formatted text field): all 36,367 window values match the pattern $#,###.00 exactly (0 blank, 0 off-pattern, 0 negative); 484 are $0.00 and 281 are $1.00 (2.1% combined); 35,586 (97.9%) state more than $1. Source-side parsed window sum = $12,753,401,142.08; largest single value $531,845,387 appears exactly once (4.2% of the sum). Stamp test: the most-repeated values above $1M are round applicant budgets ($2,000,000 x29 at 21 addresses; $1,200,000 x20) — the signature of round declared estimates, not of a system stamp; the only non-round repeats >=3x are Certificates of Occupancy restating one project's declared value at the SAME address ($8,890,000 x3 at 150 Oliver St; $3,489,000 x3 at 100 Federal St), and one odd value ($404,947,987) appears twice. Freshest issued_date in the table: 2026-10-17; the datastore resource's last_modified is 2026-10-17T19:02:00Z (daily re-upload). NOTE: the CKAN SQL endpoint throttles bursts (HTTP 403 after rapid-fire queries, recovering in a minute or two) — the adapter paces pages at 1s with hard backoff.
coverage_note: Permits issued by the City of Boston (Inspectional Services Department) only. Suffolk County also contains Chelsea, Revere, and Winthrop, which publish their permits separately and are not in this feed.

dedupe_rule.definition: One published permit = one row of the Approved Building Permits datastore, identified by its permit number (permitnumber). The trailing-12-month window's permit numbers are exactly unique, so every window row is counted once. Amendments and Certificates of Occupancy are separate permits the city issued, carrying their own permit numbers — counted as themselves, not as duplicates of the permits they amend or close out.
dedupe_rule.measurement: Trailing-12-month window (issued_date >= 2025-10-17), measured 2026-10-18 against the live CKAN datastore: 36,367 rows = 36,367 distinct permitnumber = 36,367 distinct _id. All-time, the datastore carries 666,457 rows vs 666,444 distinct permit numbers: 13 surplus legacy rows (0.002%), none of them in the issued window. The pipeline's in-batch duplicate gate and the (county_id, source_record_id) upsert key guard every future pull.
dedupe_rule.rule: source_record_id = permitnumber; count every window row once.

field_map.application_date: NOT PUBLISHED — the dataset carries no application-date column (it publishes issued and expiration dates only), so application_date stays NULL by construction
field_map.category: NOT PUBLISHED — the dataset's occupancytype is a building occupancy class (1-2FAM, Comm, Multi, 1-3FAM, Mixed, ...), not a permit category, so category stays NULL (the Chicago/SF/NYC honest-NULL treatment)
field_map.contractor_rule: NONE CARRIED — the dataset publishes exactly one name field, `applicant`, and it carries person names (verified on sampled rows: individual applicants, e.g. on residential permits). It is never requested: excluded from the pull's column list entirely. No contractor/business field exists in the schema, so contractor_name stays NULL, never inferred (the San Francisco treatment).
field_map.issue_date: issued_date (the issuance-date field; every row in the datastore carries one — the publisher includes issued permits only)
field_map.permit_type: permittypedescr (the source's own permit label, e.g. 'Short Form Bldg Permit'; falls back to worktype)
field_map.project_description: comments (the applicant's scope-of-work text) when present, else description (the source's short work label)
field_map.valuation: declared_valuation — the applicant's declared project value, published as a formatted text string ('$36,500.00'); parsed by stripping $ and commas. Validated 2026-10-18 (see audit): 100% on-pattern, 97.9% above $1, no placeholder or sibling-stamp pathology at scale (contrast Austin and Seattle), and the DB window sum must reproduce the source-side parsed sum $12,753,401,142.08 to the cent. KNOWN QUIRK (mirrored as reported, SOP rule 2 — the Chicago treatment): Certificates of Occupancy restate their project's declared value at the same address, so a project's value can appear on its building permit and again on its C-of-O; values are the source's, printed as reported.
